COLOUR CONSIDERATION FOR
GARMENTS
10.1
INTRODUCTION
Colour combination has a very important place in tailoring. It is essential for every student
of dress making as well as for all tailors to have knowledge of colour combinations in
order to use them effectively on clothes, buttons, accessories, etc. Inadequate knowledge
will result in garments with poor colour combinations which do not look good. Good
combinations make a garment look attractive, hence knowledge of colour combinations
is very important.
10.2
OBJECTIVES
After reading this lesson you will be able to:
•
explain colour schemes;
•
explain colour contrasts;
•
use colour combinations for matching cloth, thread and buttons;
•
list points to be kept in mind while using a colour scheme.
10.3
COLOUR SCHEME
All colours - whether they are primary, secondary or neutral, are used in tailoring. Black
and white are not shades of any colour. Black is the colour of mourning whereas white

1.
Primary colours

colours. These are -

Red colour
This is a very bright and attractive colour. It affects the mental state of person. As

ii)
Blue colour
It is a cool colour and is used to denote water or the sky.
iii)
Yellow colour
This is also a bright colour and is generally used at weddings, etc.
2.
Secondary colours
The colour obtained on mixing two primary colours is known as a secondary colour.
Example:-
Red of Yellow = Orange
Yellow +Blue = Green
Blue+Red=Purple
In this way we obtain three secondary colours. Some of these are cool and some are
warm. Every primary colour has three contrasts and very secondary colour has one primary
contrast, such as green has red "asthe primary contrast.
10.4

proper contrasts are used. This is also known as complementary contrast. For example'-

10.5 USINGCOLOUR~CHEMES
The following points should be kept in mind while using colour schemes :-
•
./
-
->
1:
According to the base of the garment
First of all for the base ofthe gamient, that is, the cloth should be seen because
the colours used will depend upon it. While using the colour scheme, it is best to
use one colour first and then gradually use other colours, Not more than two,or
three colours should be used in a colour scheme.
2.
According to the design
.,
Design are of many kinds. Natural colours should be used when using designs
from nature, such as birds, flowers, plants, etc. The natural colours look best on
such designs. Geometrical designs can be made in any desired colour which looks
good.
3.
According to the wearer
Bright attractive colours and nursery prints look good on children's garments.
Care should be taken while selecting colours and designs for garments of adults.
Bright colours suit children garments. Adults garment look good in dark colours
whereas older persons garments look best in light and sober colours. Hence,
colour schemes should be used according to the garment and according to the age
ofthe wearer.
4.
According to climate and tradition
Both climate and tradition have a great influence on colour schemes of garments.
Light colours are preferred in summer and dark colours in winter. If dark colours
are used in summer they hurt the eye and are not very pleasant.

10.6
COLOURHARMONY
Colour harmony refers to the harmonious and pleasing use of colour combinations. One
should never use more than five colours ifone wants to achieve colour harmony. Contrasting
colours should also be carefully selected so that a pleasant effect is achieved. Harmony
is of the following kinds.
1.
Analogous harmony
The colours which gradually merge together are used together like yellow, green
yellow and green.
2.
Monochromatic harmony -
When shades of anyone colour are used together, ranging from light to dark,
monochromatic harmony is achieved, e.g. -Iight blue and dark blue.
3.
Complementary harmony
When complementary
colours are used together it is called complementary
harmony, e.g. - yellow green is'"usedwith its complements red and purple. and
blue-purple is used with its complements yellow and red. Dark colours look good
when used in combination such as orange colour on a brown coat.
4.
Dominant harmony
Many shades of colours are used on garments and outofthose used, the dominant
colour forms the dominant harmony. Any desired colour can be higilE;r ..tedby
making an outline of its contrasting colour. For example, the yellow colour of a
frock can be highlighted by using green colour on it either as piping or as the
embroidery thread.
5.
Related harmony
When the colour formed by the combination of two primary colours, is used with
a neutral colour, related harmony is obtained. For example-
Red + Yellow = Orange
'
Related harmony - Orange + grey; orange + black; orange + white
CHARACTERISTICS OF COLOURS
